container.help: Curves f(t) that make boundary conditions vary in time. Add one curve per variation you need, then reference it by name from a boundary condition. Leaving a boundary condition set to Constant keeps the behaviour of a model without any time functions.

blockdata.name: Time function 1
blockdata.help: One curve f(t). Rename it to something meaningful: the name is what you pick from the Time variation field of a boundary condition.

value.help: ramp: linear between two points in time, held flat outside. periodic: a repeating wave. table: values read from a CSV file. constant: a flat value, useful only in multiplier mode.

absolute: this curve IS the boundary value, in the same units as the boundary condition field, and the number typed there is ignored. multiplier: the applied boundary condition is (the value typed in the boundary condition) x f(t), so f is dimensionless. Use absolute for measured data, multiplier to scale a magnitude you have already entered.
For a ramp, the time the rise begins; the value is held at the start value before it. For a periodic curve, the time the cycle is measured from.
The time the rise ends. The value is held at the end value after it. Must be greater than the start time.
Value at and before the start time, in the units of the boundary condition this curve drives.
Value at and after the end time.
All four forms peak at the mean plus the amplitude and trough at the mean minus it, so the amplitude means the same thing whichever you pick.
Value the wave oscillates about, in the units of the boundary condition.
Half the peak to trough swing.
Duration of one cycle. For a daily cycle in a model running in seconds this is 86400. Must be positive.
Phase offset in radians. Use pi/2 = 1.5708 to start at the peak instead of at the mean.

Name of a two column CSV file holding time in the first column and the boundary value in the second. Times must increase. A header row and lines beginning with # are ignored. Use the ADSIM menu, Import time series CSV, to browse for a file and copy it next to the project; then type its name here. The file is copied into the .ADSIM folder when the input files are generated.
linear: straight line between samples. step: hold each sample until the next one. The solver samples the curve at its own time step, which is independent of the spacing in the file.
What to return for times before the first row of the file. hold: the first value. zero: nothing. repeat: cycle the file. error: stop the calculation.

What to return for times past the last row of the file. hold: the last value. zero: nothing. repeat: cycle the file, which is how you drive a long run from one recorded cycle. error: stop the calculation.
Added to every time in the file after scaling. Use it to start a recorded history at a later point of the simulation.
Multiplies every time in the file. A file recorded in hours driving a model running in seconds needs 3600. Must be positive.

Integrate the curve over each time step instead of sampling it at one instant. Only meaningful on a flow boundary, where it keeps the total injected mass correct even when the time step is coarser than the spacing of the file. Leave off for prescribed values.
A curve that never changes. Mostly useful in multiplier mode to scale a boundary condition by a fixed factor.
